next_question: Does direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions, bypassing indirect behavioral/temporal signals entirely) provide reliable drift-vs-noise discrimination that all five tested indirect signal families (Jaccard, TF-IDF, response-time KS, linear ensemble, field-usage profiling) cannot?
why_next: Five indirect signal families for C-FRESHNESS drift-vs-noise discrimination have now been tested and falsified on the same mock server: (1) Jaccard structural similarity FP=1.0 under noise; (2) TF-IDF semantic similarity FP=1.0 inverted; (3) response-time KS test TP=0.0 inverted; (4) linear Fisher LDA ensemble AUC=0.625 all conditions fail; (5) field-usage profiling — orthogonal to Jaccard (r=-0.045) but fails on change_type (usage_similarity=1.0, measurement-valid limitation of availability-only counting). Each failed for a distinct root cause but the common thread is indirect behavioral/temporal signals confounded by structural complexity magnitude. The parent handoff (EXP-GRAPH-35130682058) correctly identified direct schema comparison as the highest-upside orthogonal approach — it measures structural change directly rather than via behavioral proxy. This experiment confirms that behavioral profiling provides a genuinely orthogonal signal but cannot cover all drift patterns; direct comparison remains the most promising untested alternative.

established: Field-usage profiling IS orthogonal to Jaccard structural similarity: Pearson r=-0.045 across 24 conditions (audit.json condition3_orthogonality PASS, recomputed_metrics.pearson_r_jaccard_vs_usage=-0.044548). This is the first tested signal family that achieves near-zero correlation with Jaccard, confirming the parent's recommendation to test fundamentally different signal families.

Field-usage profiling discriminates field-availability drift from structural noise: remove_field mean usage_similarity=0.865 (<0.90 threshold), required_to_optional mean usage_similarity=0.639 (<0.90), while all three noise patterns produce usage_similarity=1.0 (>=0.95 threshold). Discrimination gap=0.165 (audit.json claim_ceiling).

Field-usage profiling does NOT detect type-compatibility drift: change_type produces usage_similarity=1.0 at all 4 schema sizes because field-availability counting ignores type mismatch (audit V_CHANGE_TYPE_AVAILABILITY_ONLY). This is a measurement-definition limitation, not an inherent property of behavioral profiling — type-aware client validation was not modeled.

Five signal families tested and falsified for C-FRESHNESS frozen decision rule: Jaccard (EXP-GRAPH-34788722106), TF-IDF (EXP-GRAPH-35010853847), response-time KS (EXP-GRAPH-35083040517), linear ensemble (EXP-GRAPH-35130682058), field-usage profiling (this experiment). The broader C-FRESHNESS domain remains open — each falsification is bounded to specific settings.

Noise immunity for unused fields is a construction artefact (audit V_NOISE_TAUTOLOGICAL): all three noise generators add fields with names churn_opt_*, null_field_*, *.nested_* that no CLIENT_PROFILE requests. Real-world noise affecting used fields would close the discrimination gap. This is a ceiling value under idealization, not empirical robustness.

required_to_optional measurement is deterministic removal, not intermittent (audit V_REQUIRED_TO_OPTIONAL_DEAD_CODE): code has dead branch (both even and odd paths execute continue), making field 100% absent instead of ~50% intermittent as spec intended. Observed usage_similarity 0.639 reflects full removal, not intermittent absence.
rejected: Field-usage profiling as defined (presence-only counting) satisfies the frozen C-FRESHNESS decision rule — FALSIFIED: change_type at usage_similarity=1.0 fails Condition1 (result.json metrics.condition1_drift_detection='FAIL')
Any single indirect behavioral/temporal signal family provides complete drift-vs-noise discrimination — five families now tested, all fail frozen gate for distinct root causes
Noise patterns adding only unused fields provide a stress test of usage-similarity — tautological by construction (audit V_NOISE_TAUTOLOGICAL)
unknown: Whether type-aware client validation (rejecting fields with unexpected types) would make change_type detectable and close Condition1 gap — requires modeling type schemas and client parsing logic
Whether usage-similarity discrimination survives when noise patterns affect fields actually used by clients (not just unused churn/null/nested fields) — current noise model is adversarially favorable
Whether truly intermittent required_to_optional (field present 50% of responses) yields different usage_similarity than deterministic removal (0.639)
Whether real APIs with DB/cache/CDN, stochastic availability, and heterogeneous production client profiles preserve 0.165 discrimination gap and near-zero Jaccard correlation
Whether composite signal (Jaccard + usage_similarity + type-compatibility) could detect all three drift patterns simultaneously despite individual limitations
Per-sample (not aggregated mean) Pearson r and per-sample ROC for Jaccard vs usage-similarity — aggregation to 24 mean pairs may mask sample-level structure
Whether direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions) bypasses the indirect signal problem entirely
Whether nonlinear ensembles (SVM, random forest) on usage-similarity + Jaccard features could achieve TP>=0.8 FP<=0.15 despite single-signal failures
do_not_assume: C-FRESHNESS is globally closed or rejected — five bounded signal families falsified in specific controlled settings; the broader domain remains open (audit claim_ceiling)
Field-usage profiling is rejected as a signal — it provides valid but incomplete discrimination; the narrower signal IS orthogonal (r=-0.045) and works for field-availability drift

The discrimination gap (0.165) and near-zero correlation (r=-0.045) would hold on real APIs — these are ceiling values under deterministic mock server with hand-designed profiles and adversarially favorable noise

Direct schema comparison is required — this is a recommendation, not an established fact; other untested signal families (session tokens, schema access patterns, semantic embeddings) may still succeed
The magnitude confound (noise adds more fields than drift) is the only failure mode — change_type failure is a measurement-definition limitation (availability-only counting), not a magnitude confound
Synthetic noise patterns (10% churn, deduped nulls, single nested conversion) that add only unused fields are representative of real-world API variation
Per-sample ROC would show the same results as aggregated per-condition means — aggregation limits power and may mask discriminative structure

recommended_action: Design a graph lane experiment testing direct schema comparison (structural diff of schema definitions) as a C-FRESHNESS signal. The approach should diff schema structures (field names, types, nesting depth, required/optional status, enum constraints) between fresh and stale samples and measure whether the diff magnitude or diff type discriminates drift from noise without the magnitude confound that has affected all five tested indirect signal families. The frozen decision rule should use per-sample features (not aggregated means) with N>=30 per condition. Noise patterns should be redesigned to overlap with client-requested fields (fixing V_NOISE_TAUTOLOGICAL from this experiment). A type-aware client validation condition should be included (fixing V_CHANGE_TYPE_AVAILABILITY_ONLY). If direct schema comparison fails, pivot to session-level behavioral signals (token validation, cookie state inspection) which test a fundamentally different dimension from both structural and field-usage signals.
